summary: ARES ( Astronautic Reconnaissance & Exploration System ) is a map software for astronauts on a mars. The mission we had designed is one to Jezero Crater located on Mars. The goal of the mission is to sample sedimentary rocks there and see whether ancient materials could have supported life. The crew are equipped with a vehicle to transport them to different sites at the survey zone. The vehicle has an onboard lab to conduct research at the sites, windshields to protect them from external weather ( sandstorms, etc ) and a screen that displays this map software.  This addresses the challenge through giving astronauts a useful tool to manage safety concerns such as hazardous external weather outside of crew habitats.
details: The map tool features a planetary map of Mars, with a regional survey zone at Jezero Crater. In the regional survey zone there includes, a landing site and 3 mission sites, which includes the western section of Jezero Crater. When interacted with, each of the mission areas show imagery, descriptions and provide astronauts some background information of the site shown. On the upper-right corner of the map software, there is a topography toggle, giving crew insight on steep terrain and obstacles when en route to mission sites. On the lower-left corner of the software, there is an information panel button that displays mission objectives. Additionally, the information panel also features local weather and radiation data gathered previously by the Perseverance Rover. This benefits the crew with crucial insights on the outside environment on Mars, ensuring astronaut safety. Our intended impact is through providing an idea on how software tools and systems should look like for real space missions. We used Github to house our code, using html to create ARES. We also used online available data such as public planetary maps of mars and topographic maps of Jezero Crater taken from orbit.
